questions.prompt: Which network topology links devices through a central switch?
questions.feedback: Star endpoints use a central network device.

blocks.title: Topology describes connections
blocks.text: A network topology shows how computers and connection devices link together.

blocks.title: Star topology
blocks.text: Each endpoint connects to a central device such as a switch. Easier to add/manage devices, but the central device is a point of failure.

blocks.title: Mesh topology
blocks.text: Devices can connect to multiple others. Alternative paths make the system resilient if one link fails, but more connections increase cost and complexity.

blocks.title: Compare in context
blocks.text: For a small school LAN, a star can be practical. A high-availability network may use mesh routes; explain what happens when a link or central device fails.

blocks.title: Worked example
blocks.text: All classroom devices connect to one central switch. New devices can be connected easily [1], making the network straightforward to manage [1]. The switch is a single point of failure [1], so its failure can interrupt communication for connected devices [1]. Give advantage plus linked benefit and disadvantage plus linked effect.

items: Topology — Arrangement of network devices and links.
Star topology — Endpoints connect to a central switch or hub.
Mesh topology — Devices connect via multiple paths between nodes.
Fault tolerance — Ability to continue working after some faults.
Central switch — Network device that connects and forwards data to LAN devices.
Redundancy — Extra paths that can be used if a path fails.
